metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: The speaker has lived with the constant awareness, presence, or threat of death for a very long time, viewing it as a familiar companion rather than a terrifying stranger.
acceptable_visual_variants: A person walking down a winding path with a soft, warm shadow cast beside them that mimics a companion's form.
A person sitting peacefully looking at a gentle, stylized figure made of mist or light.
metaphor_spans.literal_meaning: I have a long-standing, literal friendship with the biological state of death.
metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: Depicting a literal human friend or a cartoonish Grim Reaper shaking hands with the speaker, which misses the psychological depth of accepting mortality.

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The translation adds the word 'firm' to rhyme with 'turn', which is not present in the original Hindi text ('ehsaas hai' simply means 'is felt' or 'is sensed').

stanzas.loss_note: The translation renders 'जो मुझसे मिलने आई है' (who has come to meet me) as 'Who comes to understand' to force a rhyme with 'hand', altering the literal meaning of the final line.

annotation.theme: The personification of death not as a terrifying end, but as a lifelong, supportive companion and friend.

original_poem:
मौत से मेरी दोस्ती पुरानी है,  
वो हर मोड़ पर मेरे साथ है,  
जिंदगी के हर पड़ाव पर,  
उसकी परछाई का एहसास है।  

जब भी मैं गिरा हूँ,  
वो हाथ पकड़ने आई है,  
मौत मेरी दोस्त है,  
जो मुझसे मिलने आई है।
translated_poem:
My friendship with death is old,  
She accompanies me at every turn,  
At every stage of life,  
Her shadow is felt, firm.

Whenever I have fallen,  
She has come to hold my hand,  
Death is my friend,  
Who comes to understand.
